blocked_route.verdict: headless Chromium NEVER clears the Cloudflare interactive challenge
blocked_route.headless_chromium: BrowserController launched exactly as production does (browser.py unmodified, headless=True). page.goto() returned HTTP 403; title 'Just a moment...'; body 28484 bytes at t=0 then frozen at 28635 bytes. Polled page.content() every 5 s for 60 s (3x the 20 s budget) - identical body every poll, URL never left /events, challenge markers (cf-chl, challenges.cloudflare.com turnstile, /cdn-cgi/challenge-platform) present throughout. A longer wait does NOT help.
blocked_route.headed_chromium: Tested ONCE locally for information only (headless=False, no stealth flags, no bypass service). First navigation to /events returned HTTP 200 and the real 261586-byte page (title '| The Faculty of Intensive Care Medicine', 9 event links, ?page=0/?page=1 pager). BUT in the same session the very next navigations - ?page=1, ?page=2 and a detail page /events/uk-shock-2026 - all returned HTTP 403 'Just a moment...'. So even headed Chromium is not a dependable route, and headed is unavailable on a GitHub runner anyway.
blocked_route.no_bypass_attempted: No stealth plugin, no UA spoofing beyond the project's existing default header, no third-party solver.

alternative_route_found.why_it_works: HTTP 200, ~104 KB, content-type application/rss+xml, cf-cache-status DYNAMIC and cache-control no-cache (so it is origin-served, not a stale edge cache). Returns 200 with ANY User-Agent tested, including the default curl UA and 'python-httpx/0.27' - so it is not UA-gated and is very likely to work from a GitHub runner IP, though that is unverified from here.
alternative_route_found.why_it_is_rich: Drupal renders each node's FULL body into <description>, so ONE feed fetch yields the listing AND every detail page: event dates as <time datetime> tags, availability, BOOK NOW url, fee <table>s, CPD points, event format and venue. No per-event fetch is needed - and none is possible.
alternative_route_found.why_coverage_is_partial: rss.xml is the 10 most recently CREATED nodes site-wide, news posts included - NOT the /events view. On 2026-09-26 it held 9 event nodes, of which only 5 were among the 9 upcoming events the real /events page 0 listed. Missing: famusfusic, fficm-oscesoe-exam-online-course-autumn-2026, getting-ready-for-the-applied-clinical-reasoning-examination-acre-0, leeds-acute-intensive-care-conference-lactic, plus everything on ?page=1.

source_row.extraction_instructions: ficm.ac.uk HTML is entirely behind an interactive Cloudflare challenge that headless Chromium never clears, so this source does NOT use the /events page at all. list_shells_override() fetches the site-wide Drupal feed https://www.ficm.ac.uk/rss.xml (not challenged) and keeps only <item>s whose <link> contains /events/. Drupal renders each node's full body into <description>, so the SAME feed fetch supplies every detail field; extract_detail() ignores the Playwright page (the scraper's navigate to booking_url lands on the 403 challenge) and parses the body stashed on the shell as _ficm_body. Gotchas: strip the field--name-created <time> first or the node's creation date is read as the event date; the structured tail is read backwards from the literal line 'Listing image' as [category, venue, format, CPD]; the trailing Drupal label 'Pricing tab title / £300' is never a real fee. COVERAGE IS PARTIAL AND DRIFTS - the feed is the 10 most recent nodes site-wide, so upcoming events fall out of it as news is published; see concerns before activating.
source_row.active_note: Left active=false deliberately - the archival drift risk in concerns[0] is a product decision for the lead, not mine.

registry_comment: FICM - Cloudflare blocks all HTML; events parsed from the unchallenged site-wide rss.xml feed (partial coverage, see extractor docstring)

probe_results.notes: 8 shells = the 9 event nodes in the feed minus essential-radiology-for-icu-and-anaesthesia-1, whose last date (2026-09-16) is past. Three events have city but no venue_name because the feed gives only a town ('Coventry', 'Birmingham') or is online-only. Two events genuinely publish no fee (uk-shock-2026, and the feed's radiology item); 'with_pricing 6' is therefore full coverage of what is published. Ran the harness three times: 8 shells every time, identical field values.

concerns: ARCHIVAL DRIFT - the biggest risk, and the reason active=false. rss.xml holds only the 10 most recently created nodes site-wide. An event that is still months away will silently fall out of the feed as FICM publishes newer news items, and the scheduler's unseen-14d rule would then archive a live event. database.archive_stale_conferences' source-health guard does NOT cover this: the scrape still succeeds, it just returns fewer shells. Before activating, either exempt source 41 from unseen-based archival or accept that FICM rows may vanish and reappear.

COVERAGE IS ~55% AND UNMEASURABLE IN CI. Only 5 of the 9 upcoming events on the real /events page 0 were in the feed on 2026-09-26, and nothing from ?page=1 ever appears. We cannot detect what we are missing from inside the scraper, because the page that would tell us is the 403 one.

NINE WASTED PAGE LOADS PER RUN. llm_agent.extract_detail_for_shell() always navigates the browser to shell['booking_url'] before calling extract_detail(); for FICM every one of those lands on the Cloudflare challenge. It is harmless (BrowserController swallows the failure and extract_detail ignores the page) but it costs ~9 pointless requests to a site that is actively refusing us. A shared-file change would fix it properly: an opt-out flag on BaseExtractor, e.g. `detail_needs_navigation = False`, honoured in llm_agent.extract_detail_for_shell. I did not make it - shared file, other agents in flight.

start_time is only recovered for events whose feed body includes a programme table (1 of 8, eeg-in-the-icu-0 -> 09:15). The feed carries no dedicated start-time field; the <time> stamps are all normalised to 12:00:00Z and are date-only signals, so start_time is left None rather than guessed.

abstract_open / abstract_deadline are never populated. No FICM item in the feed mentioned abstracts, so abstract_classifier was not wired in; add it if a future FICM conference advertises a call for abstracts.

The site's own data is internally inconsistent on one event: intensivists-in-training-conference-2026 has structured venue 'The Marriott, Manchester Piccadilly and Online' while its prose still reads 'Join us at the Mercure, Manchester'. The extractor takes the structured field for venue_name, but the LLM description repeats 'Mercure' from the prose. Not fixable from our side - FICM needs to update the copy.

The city/venue splitter uses a hard-coded UK city and organisation-keyword list (_CITY_TOKEN / _ORG_TAIL). It handled all 8 events correctly, but an unlisted town in a comma-separated venue line will land in city verbatim (acceptable) and an unlisted town on its own line will land in venue_name instead of city (minor).
Only 8 events were ever available to test against, and all 8 were used. There is no held-out sample, so novel node layouts are unproven.
Politeness: ~25 requests total to ficm.ac.uk across all probing and testing, sequential, single browser. Well inside the 60 budget.
